culture.name: Taelrik
culture.description: River-folk of the grey river valleys. Ferrymen, toll-keepers and bargemen; blunt, superstitious about water, generous to anyone who pays the ford its due.

language.name: Taelrik
language.sound: River-folk speech: clipped and throaty, heavy on k, th and rolled r, with long open "ae" vowels. Spoken low and quickly; curses are spat, blessings are drawn out.

categories.C: k kh t th dh r rh v s n m l d
categories.V: a ae e o u i

syllable_notes: No word starts with "ng" or ends in "v"
Stress on the first syllable; an apostrophe marks a dropped vowel
language.grammar: Subject–object–verb. Blessings use the wish mood (-a): ossa "may it keep". Plurals by doubling the last consonant: dhaer → dhaerr.

dictionary.meaning: may it keep (wish mood of oss-)

phrases.translation: May the grey ford keep you.
The river is watched; the high ground is watched.
phrases.usage: Old toll-house inscription: 'you are seen, pay your due.'
Serious. Not said lightly to a ferryman.

customs: Every crossing ends with a coin dropped in the river: 'paying the ford'.
Doors face the water; a house that turns its back on the river is thought unlucky.
Oaths are sworn with wet hands.
culture.food: Smoked eel, black bread, river-cress, bitter reed beer. Oiled wool coats, wide leather belts with a toll purse; ferrymen go bare-armed in all weather.

holidays.name: Low Water
holidays.description: The river is thanked and the fords re-marked with fresh stakes.

holidays.name: Lantern Night
holidays.description: Paper lanterns floated downstream for the drowned.
